proposals.text: Customers should obtain a shopping cart before proceeding with the shopping trip.
proposals.justification: The rule refers to the general shopping practice of taking a cart rather than to any particular cart location or coordinate.

proposals.text: Customers must not leave the store without their cart.
proposals.justification: The rule is about responsible cart use at store exit and does not depend on where the exit is located in a particular layout.

proposals.text: Customers must not push carts through single-file shelf aisles.
proposals.justification: The abstraction identifies narrow shelf aisles by local geometry and shelf adjacency, so it applies in any store with single-file aisles.

proposals.text: Customers must not enter a single-file shelf aisle while pushing a cart.
proposals.justification: The rule is based on entering locally narrow shelf space, not on the absolute position of that aisle in the demonstrated floor plan.

proposals.text: If a customer parks a cart, it should be left only in a spacious throughway rather than in a constrained passage.
proposals.justification: The norm uses local free-space measurements to characterize acceptable cart-staging areas instead of naming particular cells.

proposals.text: Customers must not park a cart directly beside shelves where it could block shelf access.
proposals.justification: The rule captures a general courtesy of not blocking merchandise shelves and is defined by shelf adjacency rather than coordinates.

proposals.text: A customer who parks a cart must retrieve it before leaving.
proposals.justification: The obligation concerns the general lifecycle of a borrowed cart and does not rely on where the cart was parked.

proposals.text: After leaving a cart-free single-file shelf aisle, the customer should retrieve their cart.
proposals.justification: The trigger is defined by exiting a locally identified pedestrian-only shelf aisle, making the rule transferable across different store geometries.

Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

The demonstrations are now shown in a lower-level representation that exposes distinctions hidden before (newly available: geometry). Identify the hidden distinctions and use them to define higher-level state properties and/or events (in "abstraction"), possibly hierarchically, and propose norms expressed over them. {"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}

s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: Customers must not push carts through single-file shelf aisles.
parsed.justification: The abstraction identifies narrow shelf aisles by local geometry and shelf adjacency, so it applies in any store with single-file aisles.

parsed.text: Customers must not enter a single-file shelf aisle while pushing a cart.
parsed.justification: The rule is based on entering locally narrow shelf space, not on the absolute position of that aisle in the demonstrated floor plan.

parsed.text: If a customer parks a cart, it should be left only in a spacious throughway rather than in a constrained passage.
parsed.justification: The norm uses local free-space measurements to characterize acceptable cart-staging areas instead of naming particular cells.

parsed.text: Customers must not park a cart directly beside shelves where it could block shelf access.
parsed.justification: The rule captures a general courtesy of not blocking merchandise shelves and is defined by shelf adjacency rather than coordinates.

parsed.text: A customer who parks a cart must retrieve it before leaving.
parsed.justification: The obligation concerns the general lifecycle of a borrowed cart and does not rely on where the cart was parked.

parsed.text: After leaving a cart-free single-file shelf aisle, the customer should retrieve their cart.
parsed.justification: The trigger is defined by exiting a locally identified pedestrian-only shelf aisle, making the rule transferable across different store geometries.
